title: Paid social
hired_for: An owner hires the paid social expert to put the right message in front of the right customer at the right time, so the ad account returns the most gross profit per dollar spent.

jobs.job: Cut the ad sets that lose money, every week
jobs.why: Losing ad sets keep spending until someone stops them. Every week they run at 2x the target cost per purchase is gross profit handed to Meta.

watch.metric: share of spend in ad sets above the target cost per purchase after spending 3x that target, 7 day click, trailing 7 days

drives.metric: gross profit per ad dollar (first order gross profit divided by spend)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 35% of spend sits in ad sets at 1.9x the target cost per purchase. After: under 10% within 14 days, the rest moved to ad sets under target.

jobs.job: Check Meta's numbers against what the store actually made before scaling
jobs.why: Meta counts some sales that would have happened anyway. Scaling on Meta's own return alone can grow spend while real profit falls.

watch.metric: gap between Meta-reported purchase value and store new customer revenue, trailing 30 days

drives.metric: new customer revenue per ad dollar across all channels

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Meta says 3.1x, the store's own numbers say 1.8x. After: the gap is known each week, attribution is set to 7 day click everywhere, and scale calls use the store number.

jobs.job: Stop spending on products that are about to sell out
jobs.why: Ads that keep pushing a product with a week of stock left burn money on buyers who cannot buy, then leave a stockout and a cold ad account.

watch.metric: ad spend on products with under 14 days of stock, trailing 7 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and Shopify inventory

drives.metric: wasted spend and lost orders from stockouts

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $4,200 last week went to 2 products with 6 days of stock. After: that spend moves to in-stock winners before the stock runs out.
jobs.who_today: nobody, or the founder by chance

jobs.job: Find the one thing holding the account back before spending more
jobs.why: Owners raise budget when the real limit is a tired ad, a weak page or broken tracking. Fixing the wrong thing wastes a month.

watch.metric: cost per purchase split into cost per 1,000 views, click rate and page conversion rate, trailing 14 days, each against the account's own 90 day level

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: cost per purchase up 30% and the plan is new audiences. After: the split shows page conversion fell from 3.1% to 2.2%; the page gets fixed first.

jobs.job: Keep spend on pace for the month's budget and profit target
jobs.why: Overspending early in the month or under-spending into a good week both miss the profit plan. The owner wants to know today, not at month end.

watch.metric: month to date spend against plan, and gross profit after ad spend against plan

drives.metric: month end gross profit after ad spend

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 62% of the month's budget spent by day 15. After: daily pace shown against plan; month lands within 5% of budget.
jobs.who_today: media buyer or founder with a spreadsheet

jobs.job: Catch a sudden jump in spend or cost and find the cause the same day
jobs.why: A broken pixel, a rejected ad or a site outage can burn a day of budget. Found the next week, it has already cost thousands.

watch.metric: daily spend and cost per purchase against the last 14 day range

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a checkout bug ran 2 days before anyone saw purchases drop. After: flagged within hours, with the 3 ads and the likely cause named.
jobs.who_today: nobody, or the media buyer next morning

jobs.job: Agree how much a new customer is allowed to cost
jobs.why: Without a ceiling, scaling stops too early or runs past the point where first orders make money. The ceiling must come from margin and repeat buying.

watch.metric: first order gross profit divided by cost per new customer, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no written ceiling; buyers target a return of 2x on every product. After: a $38 ceiling set from margin and 90 day repeat, reviewed monthly.

jobs.job: Scale winning ad sets in steps without breaking them
jobs.why: Doubling a winner overnight often resets it and wastes the win. Scaling in steps and moving proven winners to a scaling campaign keeps them working.

watch.metric: new customer purchases from ad sets whose budget was raised, cost per purchase 7 day click, trailing 7 days after each raise

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 winners were doubled and both lost 40% of their return. After: step raises every read window, winners hold within 10% of target at 2x spend.

jobs.job: Grow new customers, not just re-buy the old ones
jobs.why: Ads can look great by selling to past customers who would have come back anyway. The business only grows if the spend finds new buyers.

watch.metric: new customer share of orders from Meta traffic, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Shopify first order flag and Meta Ads Manager

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 41% of Meta driven orders are from returning customers. After: past buyers excluded from cold campaigns, new customer share up to 70%.

jobs.job: Keep ads approved and the ad account safe
jobs.why: Rejected ads and account warnings stop delivery and can close the account. Lost logins leave the business locked out of its own ads.

watch.metric: rejected ads and open account quality warnings, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 7 rejections last month for the same claim, 1 admin with sole access. After: the pattern is fixed at the source and 2 admins hold access.

jobs.job: Spot tired ads before they drag the cost up
jobs.why: When the same people see an ad too often, cost per purchase creeps up slowly. Found late, the account has no fresh ads ready to take over.

watch.metric: times each person saw the ad in 30 days, by audience, next to cost per purchase trend of the top 5 ads

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the top ad is at 4.8 views per person with reach flat and cost up 25%. After: flagged at 3.5, a new version of the ad ready before cost rises.

jobs.job: Test new ads the right way so each test gives an answer
jobs.why: Tests with too little spend or tiny changes end with 'not sure'. The owner pays for tests and wants a clear yes or no.

watch.metric: share of tests read after spending at least 3x the target cost per purchase and 7 days, with a winner rule written first, trailing 90 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and brand brain test log

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: half of tests were judged on under $100 of spend. After: every test has a written rule and enough spend; 1 in 5 finds a winner.

jobs.job: Keep past customers and catalog ads out of the budget meant for new buyers
jobs.why: Retargeting and catalog ads take the cheapest sales and can eat the cold budget. Read on the wrong window, they look better than they are.

watch.metric: share of spend on existing customers and catalog ads, trailing 30 days, with catalog ads read on 7 day click

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: catalog ads share the cold campaign and take 28% of spend. After: own ad set capped at 10%, cold cost per new customer down 12%.

jobs.job: Make sure the ad and the landing page say the same thing
jobs.why: A winning headline that the page does not repeat loses buyers after the click. The best ads change often and pages fall behind.

watch.metric: bounce rate of Meta traffic on the landing page, trailing 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the top ad's headline has not been on the page for 12 days. After: page updated within a day of a new winner, Meta bounce down from 68% to 58%.

jobs.job: Plan the ramp into a big sale and the wind-down after it
jobs.why: Budget raised too late misses the sale. Budget left high after it burns money on buyers who already bought.

watch.metric: cost per purchase during the sale window against plan, 7 day click

drives.metric: sale period gross profit after ad spend

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: last Black Friday budget rose on the day and stayed high 5 days after. After: ramp starts 10 days out and a wind-down date is set in advance.

jobs.job: Set spend targets per product from each product's own margin
jobs.why: One return target for the whole store overfunds low-margin products and starves high-margin ones.

watch.metric: ad spend on products below their own break-even return, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and Shopify product margins

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 35% margin gift set gets the same 2x target as a 70% margin pack. After: targets by product; $3,000 a month moves to the higher-margin line.

jobs.job: Show the owner which calls need them, and why
jobs.why: Big moves like a large budget raise or a new offer need the founder. Mixed in with daily noise they wait for days or get made without a yes.

watch.metric: decisions waiting on the founder for more than 48 hours

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 decisions sit in a chat thread, the oldest 9 days. After: 1 list, each with its cost of waiting, cleared within 2 days.

jobs.job: Keep every order and its value flowing back to Meta
jobs.why: If Meta does not see all purchases or their value, it finds the wrong buyers and every number on the screen is off.

watch.metric: share of store orders Meta records with the right value, and event match quality, trailing 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Meta sees 72% of orders and match quality is 5.8. After: 92% of orders with value, match quality above 8.

jobs.job: Keep a steady flow of new ads so spend never runs out of winners
jobs.why: Accounts that launch new ads only now and then stall when the top ad tires. A steady pace, sized to spend, keeps winners coming.

watch.metric: new ads launched per $1,000 of monthly spend, trailing 30 days

drives.metric: share of spend on ads under 30 days old

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 12 new ads on $60,000 spend, 0.2 per $1,000. After: close to 1 per $1,000 across enough distinct concepts for the spend level.

jobs.job: Test Meta's suggestions before saying yes to them
jobs.why: Meta's suggested changes and automatic edits can distort product images and shift spend in ways nobody logged. Some help, some cost money.

watch.metric: suggestions applied with no test on record, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Meta account activity log and brand brain test log

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 automatic creative edits are on across product ads. After: all off by default; each suggestion runs as a logged test first.

jobs.job: Stop paying for placements and settings that do not fit our stage
jobs.why: Some placements and bid settings bring cheap views that never buy. They hide inside blended numbers.

watch.metric: share of spend on low value placements such as app network, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9% of spend runs on app network placements with 0.2% of purchases. After: removed, cost per purchase down 5%.

jobs.job: Keep the account built simply enough to read and learn from
jobs.why: Too many small campaigns split the data so nothing learns. The owner cannot tell what each campaign is for.

watch.metric: live campaigns and ad sets per $10,000 of monthly spend, and share with a written purpose
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and brand brain

drives.metric: stability of cost per purchase week to week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 14 campaigns on $40,000 a month, 3 with a purpose on file. After: 4 campaigns, each with a one-line reason.

jobs.job: Run a lift test when Meta and the store still disagree
jobs.why: When the gap between Meta and the store will not close, only a test with a held-out group shows what Meta really adds.

watch.metric: extra purchases per $1 of spend from a lift test

drives.metric: new customer revenue per ad dollar

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Meta claims 3x, store numbers suggest 1.5x, nobody knows which. After: a 4 week lift test shows 2.1x and sets the scale ceiling.

jobs.job: Spend on new ads only what the account's hit rate can pay back
jobs.why: Production costs money. Too little and winners run out; too much and ads that never run eat the profit.

watch.metric: production cost per winning ad, trailing 90 days
watch.source: brand brain production log and Meta Ads Manager

drives.metric: gross profit per ad dollar, including production

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $9,000 a month on video, 1 winner in 3 months. After: more statics to test angles first, cost per winner down from $27,000 to $6,000.

jobs.job: Launch and scale TikTok the right way when the brand is ready
jobs.why: TikTok needs its own setup, tests and reads. Copying Meta settings wastes the first budget.

watch.metric: TikTok cost per purchase on 7 day click, checked against store orders, trailing 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: TikTok spends $3,000 a month with no pixel check. After: pixel verified, 2 ad groups by 3 ads test, cost per purchase within 20% of Meta.
